records.text: The words of Amos that came among nakkarim from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

The ravine of My mountains will be blocked; the mountain ravine will be joined as far as Iasol and blocked as it was blocked in the days of the earthquake, in the days of Oziah king of Judah. The Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him.
He said: “The Lord spoke from Zion and gave His voice from Jerusalem; the shepherds’ pastures mourned, and Carmel’s summit dried up.”
The Lord will cry out from Zion and give His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare His people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.
The Lord said: “For three impieties of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sawed the pregnant women of those in Gilead with iron saws.

Hazael said, ‘Why does my lord weep?’ He said, ‘Because I know all the evils you will do to the sons of Israel: you will send their strongholds into fire, kill their chosen men with the sword, dash down their infants, and tear open their pregnant women.’
I will send fire into Hazael’s house, and it will devour the foundations of the son of Ader,
I will kindle fire in Damascus’s wall, and it will devour the quarters of Ader’s son.

and I will shatter Damascus’s bars and destroy inhabitants from the Plain of On. I will cut down a tribe from the men of Harran, and the people of Syria, called by name, will be taken captive,” says the Lord.
The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from the cities and become a ruin,
abandoned for everlasting time, a bed and resting place for flocks, with no one pursuing.

There will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, nor a kingdom in Damascus, and the Syrians’ remainder will perish; for you are no better than Israel’s sons and their glory. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they took Solomon’s captives into captivity, to shut them up in Idumea.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn away from her, because they shut Solomon’s captives up in Idumea and did not remember a covenant of brothers.
I will send fire upon Gaza’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.
I will send fire upon Tyre’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.”
I will destroy inhabitants from Azotus, and a tribe will be removed from Ascalon. I will bring My hand against Accaron, and the remaining foreigners will perish,” says the Lord.
Foreigners will dwell in Azotus, and I will bring down the foreigners’ arrogance.
and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so as to thrust them out of their own borders.
Tyre built herself fortifications, stored silver like dust and gathered gold like the mud of the roads.
Therefore the Lord will inherit her and strike her strength into the sea; she will be consumed by fire.

Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Idumea, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they pursued his brother with a sword; he ravaged a womb upon the earth, seized his shuddering as testimony, and kept his onrush for victory.
because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.
I will send fire into Teman, and it will devour the foundations of her walls.”

Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.

Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they ripped open the pregnant women of the Gileadites in order to enlarge their borders.
Then Manaem struck Thersa, everything in it, and its territory from Thersa, because they did not open to him. He struck it and ripped open the pregnant women.
I will kindle fire upon Rabbah’s walls, and it will devour her foundations with shouting on the day of war; she will be shaken on the day of her end.

Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the din of wars heard against Rabbath. They will become an untrodden place and a destruction, her altars will be burned with fire, and Israel will receive his rule.
Her kings will go into captivity, their priests and their rulers together,” says the Lord.

Shout aloud, Heshbon, for Gai perished! Cry out, daughters of Rabbath; put on sackcloth, be seized with distress, and beat yourselves over Melchom, for he will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.

triples.relationship: related regnal references to an earthquake
triples.rationale: Amos dates its words two years before an earthquake during Uzziah's reign in Judah. Zechariah compares a blocked ravine with its blocking in the earthquake in the days of Oziah king of Judah. The earthquake and royal dating supply the comparison; the given name forms and the different uses of the event are preserved.
triples.source_text: The words of Amos that came among nakkarim from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

triples.relationship: close pairing of the Lord's voice from Zion and Jerusalem
triples.rationale: Both passages pair the Lord's voice from Zion with His voice from Jerusalem. Amos describes mourning pastures and a dried Carmel summit, while Joel describes shaking heaven and earth and the Lord sparing and strengthening His people. The opening declaration closely corresponds despite the different consequences.

target_units.text: The Lord will cry out from Zion and give His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare His people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.

triples.relationship: related Syrian violence against pregnant women
triples.rationale: Amos condemns Damascus for sawing pregnant women in Gilead with iron saws. Elisha tells Hazael of the evil he will do to Israel, including tearing open pregnant women; the surrounding account names his future Syrian kingship. The particular atrocity connects them, while method, location and reported versus predicted action differ.

triples.relationship: parallel fire consuming buildings associated with Ader's son
triples.rationale: Amos threatens fire in Hazael's house that consumes the foundations of the son of Ader. Jeremiah threatens fire in Damascus's wall that consumes the quarters of Ader's son. The named designation and consuming fire are shared; foundations and quarters remain the supplied building descriptions.

triples.relationship: parallel judgment removing Damascus's strength and affecting Syria
triples.rationale: Amos announces shattered Damascus bars and the captivity of Syria's people, alongside other named removals. Isaiah announces ruined Damascus, the loss of its kingdom and the perishing of the Syrians' remainder. Both connect Damascus's collapse with Syria's fate, while captivity and perishing are different outcomes.

triples.relationship: same-chapter paired accusations concerning Solomon's captives and Idumea
triples.rationale: The Gaza accusation describes taking Solomon's captives into captivity to shut them up in Idumea. The Tyre accusation likewise names Solomon's captives shut up in Idumea, adding the forgotten covenant of brothers. The unusual captive designation and destination connect the charges without asserting one shared incident.

triples.relationship: same-chapter repeated fire judgment upon walls and foundations
triples.rationale: The sentence against Gaza and the sentence against Tyre both announce God sending fire upon the city's walls and consuming its foundations. The repeated complete judgment formula gives the two separate city oracles a particular structural correspondence.
triples.source_text: I will send fire upon Gaza’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.

target_units.text: I will send fire upon Tyre’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.”

triples.relationship: different announced outcomes involving Azotus and foreigners
triples.rationale: Amos announces destruction of Azotus's inhabitants and the perishing of the remaining foreigners. Zechariah announces foreigners dwelling in Azotus and the bringing down of their arrogance. The city and foreigners language connect the oracles, while dwelling and destruction are not treated as the same outcome.
triples.source_text: I will destroy inhabitants from Azotus, and a tribe will be removed from Ascalon. I will bring My hand against Accaron, and the remaining foreigners will perish,” says the Lord.

triples.relationship: related accusations against Tyre concerning captives
triples.rationale: Amos condemns Tyre for confining Solomon's captives in Idumea and forgetting a covenant of brothers. Joel's address to Tyre and the other named regions condemns selling Judah and Jerusalem's sons to the Greeks. Both accuse Tyre concerning captives; confinement, sale and the supplied destinations remain distinct.

triples.relationship: parallel fire judgment upon fortified Tyre
triples.rationale: Amos threatens fire on Tyre's walls that will consume her foundations. Zechariah describes Tyre building fortifications and announces that she will be consumed by fire. The named fortified city and fiery judgment connect the oracles, while Zechariah also describes her wealth and strength struck into the sea.

triples.relationship: parallel condemnation of Idumea for violence toward a brother
triples.rationale: Amos condemns Idumea for pursuing a brother with a sword, amid its other violent acts. Obadiah condemns slaughter and impiety toward brother Jacob within its address to Idumea. Violence against a brother is shared, while Obadiah explicitly names Jacob.

triples.relationship: parallel divine judgment upon Teman's habitations
triples.rationale: Amos threatens fire consuming Teman's wall foundations. Jeremiah names the Lord's purpose against Teman's inhabitants and says their dwelling will be made untrodden. Teman and the ruin of its inhabited structures connect the judgments; fire is explicit in Amos.

triples.relationship: parallel atrocity of ripping open pregnant women
triples.rationale: Amos condemns Ammon's sons for ripping open Gileadite pregnant women to enlarge their borders. Kings reports Manaem striking Thersa and ripping open pregnant women because the place did not open to him. The particular violent act is shared, with different perpetrators, places and stated motives.

triples.relationship: parallel fire and the din of war in the Ammon oracles
triples.rationale: Amos joins fire against Rabbah's walls and foundations with shouting on the day of war. Jeremiah's Ammon oracle joins the din of wars against Rabbath with burned altars and destruction. War noise and fire connect them; the supplied place forms and burned structures remain distinct.

triples.relationship: close collective deportation of priests and rulers with a leading figure
triples.rationale: Amos says her kings will go into captivity with their priests and rulers. Jeremiah says Melchom will go into deportation with his priests and rulers. The collective priest-and-ruler deportation closely corresponds, while Amos's plural kings are not silently identified with the target's named Melchom.
